readout.measuredTooltip: Actual decoded texture footprint, measured by a real WebGL render — differs from the declared estimate when the manifest size ≠ the image's real pixels. Not a savings; a different quantity.
readout.mipCeilingTooltip: Upper bound if mipmaps are enabled (Pixi/Phaser autoGenerateMipmaps): base × 4/3 (+33%). A ceiling, not asserted residency — disabled mipmaps cost nothing here.
readout.deltaTooltip: Two measurements, not a saving: declared = manifest atlas geometry, measured = real decoded pixels from a WebGL render. The signed difference is the gap between the two methods, never a savings.
dropzone.title: Drop an asset folder to diagnose
dropzone.subtitle: TexturePacker / Pixi atlases + loose images. Analysis runs locally — nothing leaves your device.
dropzone.footnote: disk weight ≠ GPU footprint · VRAM = w × h × 4
error.noFiles: No .json or image files found there.
folder.title: Folder report
report.noAssets: No individual image or atlas assets to display.
report.noImage: No image to display for this asset.
findings.title: Findings
triage.sort.label: Sort
find.occupancy.title: Atlas {occ:pct} packed — {wasted:pct} wasted
find.occupancy.detail: {frames} frames cover {occ:pct} of {w}×{h}. Tighter packing shrinks the sheet and the VRAM it pins ({vram:bytes}). Largest contiguous empty hole is {largestPct:pct} of the sheet (dispersion {frag:pct}); the lower the dispersion, the more a full repack — not a trim — is needed.
find.occupancy.fix: Repack with MaxRects + trim, or split into a smaller sheet.
find.oversize.title: Oversized {w}×{h} (edge {edge}px)
find.oversize.detail: Longest edge {edge}px exceeds the {budget}px {sev:sev} budget. It pins {vram:bytes} of VRAM and may exceed low-end GPU limits.
find.oversize.fix: Downscale, split, or stream; verify the max texture size of your target GPUs.
find.npot.title: Non-power-of-two {w}×{h}
find.npot.detail: Padding to {potW}×{potH} would waste {waste:pct} ({vram:bytes}) IF your toolchain pads to POT. WebGL2/PixiJS upload NPOT natively (clamp+linear), so this is usually harmless.
find.npot.fix: Only act if your pipeline forces POT: trim/resize so the padding is minimal.
find.solid-fill.title: Solid {w}×{h} — one color pinning {vram:bytes}
find.solid-fill.detail: Every sampled pixel is the same color (or fully transparent) — no edges, gradient or detail. It still pins {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({w}×{h}×4) to carry a single value.
find.solid-fill.fix: Replace with a 1×1 texture tinted/stretched at runtime, or a solid-color sprite.
find.wasted-alpha.title: {srcLabel} carries an unused alpha channel — {saved:bytes} of dead weight
find.wasted-alpha.detail: Every pixel is fully opaque (alpha 255), yet this {srcLabel} still stores an alpha channel. Dropping it (re-encode opaque, same format) cuts ~{saved:bytes} ({frac:pct}) of DOWNLOAD. This is a DISK saving only — the GPU still decodes to RGBA8888, so VRAM is unchanged.
find.wasted-alpha.fix: Re-encode opaque (RGB) for delivery, or switch to a format without an alpha channel.
find.wasted-regions.detail: ≈{pct:pct} of the atlas is empty space (grid-mapped), largest contiguous hole {largestPct:pct} of the sheet.
find.format.title: {target} would cut {frac:pct}
find.format.detail: {srcLabel} {srcBytes:bytes} → {target} ~{bestBytes:bytes} (−{saved:bytes}). Canvas estimate; lossless parity needs wasm codecs.
find.format.fix: Transcode to AVIF (or WebP) for delivery.
find.format-lossless.title: {target} (lossless) suits this {contentClass}
find.format-lossless.detail: {contentClass} compresses better lossless — lossy q0.9 would fray hard edges. Prefer lossless {target}. Lossy estimate −{saved:bytes}; the Pro fix encodes lossless, so bytes will differ.

find.frame-redundancy.detail.one: {dupes} frame in {groups} group(s) have byte-identical pixel regions within this atlas. They pin {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that a de-duplicated repack reclaims, plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).
find.frame-redundancy.detail.other: {dupes} frames in {groups} group(s) have byte-identical pixel regions within this atlas. They pin {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that a de-duplicated repack reclaims, plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).

find.frame-redundancy.fix: Reference one shared frame instead of packing identical copies, or repack de-duplicated.

find.trim-margin.detail.one: {sprites} untrimmed sprite carries transparent margins around their opaque art. That padding pins {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that a trimmed repack reclaims up to, plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).
find.trim-margin.detail.other: {sprites} untrimmed sprites carry transparent margins around their opaque art. That padding pins {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that a trimmed repack reclaims up to, plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).

find.trim-margin.fix: Repack with trim enabled so each frame is tightened to its opaque bounds.

find.cross-atlas-redundancy.title.one: {dupes} duplicate frame across {sheets} atlases — identical pixels on separate sheets
find.cross-atlas-redundancy.title.other: {dupes} duplicate frames across {sheets} atlases — identical pixels on separate sheets

find.cross-atlas-redundancy.detail.one: {dupes} frame in {groups} group(s) have byte-identical pixel regions shared across {sheets} atlases ({atlases}). They pin {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that referencing one shared copy reclaims (the duplicate-frame area — separate from any empty-space merge win), plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).
find.cross-atlas-redundancy.detail.other: {dupes} frames in {groups} group(s) have byte-identical pixel regions shared across {sheets} atlases ({atlases}). They pin {vram:bytes} of VRAM ({area}px × 4) that referencing one shared copy reclaims (the duplicate-frame area — separate from any empty-space merge win), plus ~{disk:bytes} of atlas disk (area estimate).

find.cross-atlas-redundancy.fix: Reference one shared copy across the sheets instead of packing identical frames on each.

find.font-glyph-page.title.one: {glyphs} glyph on a BMFont page — {occ:pct} packed
find.font-glyph-page.title.other: {glyphs} glyphs on a BMFont page — {occ:pct} packed

find.font-glyph-page.detail.one: {face}: {glyphs} glyphs cover {occ:pct} of the {w}×{h} glyph page ({vram:bytes} of VRAM, w×h×4), with {kerning} kerning pair. A sparse glyph sheet pins that VRAM for mostly-empty space.
find.font-glyph-page.detail.other: {face}: {glyphs} glyphs cover {occ:pct} of the {w}×{h} glyph page ({vram:bytes} of VRAM, w×h×4), with {kerning} kerning pairs. A sparse glyph sheet pins that VRAM for mostly-empty space.

find.font-glyph-page.fix: Repack the glyphs tighter, drop unused characters, or generate a smaller page for the used charset.
find.duplicate-exact.title: {n}× identical file
find.duplicate-exact.detail: Byte-identical copies: {refs}. Keep one and reference it — each copy is also a separate texture upload ({vram:bytes} VRAM each).
find.duplicate-exact.fix: De-duplicate: keep a single copy and update references.
find.duplicate-similar.title: {n} near-identical images
find.duplicate-similar.detail: Perceptually near-identical (dHash ≤ {bits} bits): {refs}. Likely re-exports or near-dupes — consider reusing one.
find.should-atlas.title: {n} loose sprites — pack into an atlas
find.should-atlas.detail: {n} standalone images (≤{edge}px). Each is its own texture bind + draw call at runtime; packing them into one atlas batches the draws.
find.should-atlas.fix: Pack loose sprites into a TexturePacker / Pixi atlas.
find.atlas-merge.title: {n} under-filled atlases → merge into ~{merged}

find.atlas-merge.detail.one: {refs} are each under {pct}% full. Their content fits in ~{merged} sheet — merging cuts texture binds, draw calls and VRAM. Largest contiguous empty hole is {largestPct:pct} of its sheet (dispersion {frag:pct}); the lower the dispersion, the more a full repack — not a trim — is needed.
find.atlas-merge.detail.other: {refs} are each under {pct}% full. Their content fits in ~{merged} sheets — merging cuts texture binds, draw calls and VRAM. Largest contiguous empty hole is {largestPct:pct} of its sheet (dispersion {frag:pct}); the lower the dispersion, the more a full repack — not a trim — is needed.

find.integrity.title: Missing atlas image: {image}
find.integrity.detail: Manifest {manifest} references "{image}", which is not in the folder — the atlas can't load.
find.integrity.fix: Add the missing image or fix the manifest path.
find.format-aggregate.title: {n} images could shrink — {saved:bytes} total
find.format-aggregate.detail: Transcoding {n} images to AVIF/WebP saves ~{saved:bytes} of download across the folder.
find.variants.title: Format/resolution variants inflate VRAM
find.variants.detail: {variantFiles} variant files across {groups} logical images. At runtime one variant loads per image, so GPU VRAM is ~{loadedMin:bytes}–{loadedMax:bytes} (one resolution tier), not {summed:bytes}. Format variants (png/webp/avif) are identical in VRAM — ship one per platform; resolution variants load one tier per device.
find.variants.fix: Serve one format per platform and one resolution tier per device; don’t treat all variants as concurrent VRAM.
corr.batching.title: {drawCalls} draw calls/frame — sprites aren't batching
corr.batching.static_loose: {looseN} loose sprites not packed into an atlas
corr.batching.diag_loose: Each texture forces its own draw call — the renderer can't batch across the loose sprites.
corr.batching.diag_atlases: Each texture forces its own draw call — the renderer can't batch across the separate atlases.
corr.batching.fix_loose: Pack the loose sprites into one atlas so they batch into a single draw.
corr.batching.fix_atlases: Re-pack the atlases together so sprites share a texture and batch.
corr.vram.title: Live VRAM {live:mb} exceeds the loaded estimate
corr.vram.diag: More textures are on the GPU than the loaded set implies — textures not freed, or extra variants/atlases resident at once.
corr.vram.fix: Free off-screen textures; keep one resolution/format tier per device.
corr.upload-hitch.title: {uploads} texture uploads during gameplay
corr.upload-hitch.diag: Uploading textures to the GPU during play stalls the frame.
corr.upload-hitch.fix: Pre-upload these textures on the loading screen (GPU pre-warm).
corr.shader-hitch.title: {compiles} shaders compiled during gameplay
corr.shader-hitch.diag: Shader compilation mid-game causes a one-time hitch.
corr.redundant-state.title: ~{perFrame} redundant binds/frame
corr.redundant-state.diag: Re-binding the already-bound texture/program wastes GPU state changes.
corr.redundant-state.fix: Sort draws by texture/material so the batcher can dedupe binds.
corr.batching.title_measured: {drawCalls} → {drawCallsAfter} draw calls — measured on this device
corr.batching.static_measured: the applied fix repacked the probed sheets
corr.batching.runtime_measured: measured {drawCalls} → {drawCallsAfter} draw calls after the fix
corr.batching.diag_measured: Re-probing the repacked sheets on your GPU issued fewer draw calls — sprites now batch.
corr.batching.fix_measured: Ship the repacked sheets; this batching win is measured, not estimated.
corr.vram.static_measured: the applied fix re-probed the sheets on your GPU
corr.vram.runtime_measured: measured decoded VRAM {decodedBefore:mb} → {decodedAfter:mb} after the fix
corr.vram.diag_measured: The repacked sheets decode to less GPU texture memory on this device — distinct from the w·h·4 disk-side estimate.
corr.vram.fix_measured: Ship the repacked sheets; this decoded-VRAM reading is device-local, not a cross-device guarantee.
corr.summaryNone: No static↔runtime issues correlated — folder structure and live workload look consistent.
fix.plan.empty: Nothing to change — this folder is already clean.
fix.plan.deferredNote: Measured-now savings are only the deltas knowable before running (transcode disk is a lossy q0.9 estimate, marked ~, and may differ from the lossless Pro encode; resize VRAM is exact). Repack/merge/pack/dedup/tier sizes are computed at download. Byte and VRAM savings are distinct (disk weight ≠ GPU footprint). The references-changed flag is a prediction (a PNG fallback may still be a drop-in), and resolution tiers are an upper bound; some checks run only at execute time.
fix.plan.noneSelected: Nothing selected — choose at least one operation to run.
fix.plan.allDeselected: Nothing selected — running now would change nothing.
fix.migrate.title: Update your loader
fix.migrate.note: This fix changed which files your game loads. Repoint the load calls below — old references are shown as comments. Copy the snippet for your engine.
fix.packWarn: Packed loose images into sheets — your game must load the sheet manifest(s)/atlas, not the individual files
fix.pack.title: Pack loose images into spritesheets
fix.pack.spinePng: Spine sheets are PNG by default for runtime safety
fix.pack.inlineWarn: Packing rebuilds references — your game must load the new sheet/atlas, not the loose files. Not a drop-in replacement.
fix.pack.mode.label: Grouping mode
fix.pack.grouping.label: Static grouping
fix.pack.receipt: Packed {regions} loose images into {sheets} sheets across {groups} groups
fix.pack.verified: Spine paths: {verified} verified · {unmatched} unmatched · {unverified} not verified
fix.pack.vramDelta: Sheets add up to +{bytes:bytes} VRAM (POT padding) — the win is fewer draw calls / texture binds, not VRAM
fix.polygonHint: Interlocks concave sprites; rectangular art falls back automatically
fix.meshNote: % shown is the measured packing win. Overdraw savings need an engine-side mesh (opt-in).
fix.extrudeHint: Replicates each sprite's edge pixels {px}px into the packing gutter — stops bilinear/mipmap seams. Adds a symmetric gutter, so a sheet can grow to the next power-of-two (more VRAM, shown below).
fix.extrudeVramDelta: Edge-extrude's gutter grew a sheet by +{bytes:bytes} VRAM (next power-of-two) — the seam fix is not free

fix.extrudeSkipped.one: {n} meshed/rotated sprite skipped — no polygon-edge extrude in v1
fix.extrudeSkipped.other: {n} meshed/rotated sprites skipped — no polygon-edge extrude in v1

fix.settings.title: Optimization settings
fix.settings.effortHint: 0 = fast · 6 = max. Max effort is much slower, especially for AVIF.
fix.settings.scaleAwareHint: Lower quality on downscaled output, where detail is already lost.
fix.settings.nearLosslessHint: Near-lossless WebP — sharper than lossy, smaller than fully lossless.
fix.settings.pngRecompressHint: Re-pack PNG bytes losslessly (oxipng). Loads a codec on first use.
fix.settings.opaqueAlphaHint: Re-encode fully-opaque images without their dead alpha channel — a download/disk saving only. VRAM is unchanged (the GPU still decodes to RGBA8888).
fix.settings.bestFormatHint: Transcode each image to the format our audit measured smallest (WebP vs AVIF), instead of one format for all. A download/disk saving only — VRAM is unchanged (both decode to RGBA8888).
fix.settings.overridesHint: Override format or quality for a folder prefix or an asset type.
fix.skipped.whyNoKernel: Downscale kernel isn't configurable in-browser — the browser's high-quality resampler is used.
fix.skipped.whyNoPreBlur: Pre-blur prefilter has no in-browser equivalent; omitted (minor shimmer risk below 0.5× scale).
fix.skipped.whyNoPngquant: Lossy PNG quantization is unavailable in-browser — enable the opt-in pngquant backend (a smaller download, no GPU/VRAM change), or use WebP/AVIF.
fix.skipped.whyNoChroma: AVIF chroma subsampling toggle is held until its mapping is verified.
fix.bundles.title: Bundles
fix.bundles.hint: Bundle marking only affects which copy is kept when deduping across multi-folder packs.
fix.lazy.note: Unmarked bundles are treated as self-contained (isolated) — their duplicates are only merged within the same bundle. Mark a bundle ‘eager’ (globally resident before everything) to let other bundles share its copies. Lazy bundles stay self-contained.

fix.dedup.referencesRewritten.one: {n} reference repointed to a shared copy
fix.dedup.referencesRewritten.other: {n} references repointed to a shared copy

fix.dedup.looseSkipped.one: {n} duplicate kept — its reference may live in game code
fix.dedup.looseSkipped.other: {n} duplicates kept — their references may live in game code

fix.dedup.vramUpperBound: up to −{bytes:bytes} VRAM (upper bound — only if the runtime shares one upload across the copies)
fix.sheetDiff.proofNote: Before/after X-ray of each repacked sheet. The after-film glows red where space is still empty. OCC/VRAM/dims are two measured states, not a saving.
fix.sheetDiff.measuredBadge: measured on your GPU this run
fix.tier.title: Generate resolution tiers
fix.tier.hint: Emit downscaled copies of each asset so the game loads the resolution that fits the device.
fix.tier.inlineWarn: Tiers require resolution-aware loading. The source becomes the top tier. Not a drop-in replacement.
fix.tierWarn: Generated resolution tiers per asset — your game's loader must select the right tier at runtime (e.g. by devicePixelRatio / screen size). Source files were renamed to the top tier.
fix.tier.diskNote: Total disk grows (every tier is shipped) — this is expected. The win is per-device download and per-device VRAM, not total disk.
fix.tier.repackNote: Assets that get repacked, merged, or packed are not also tiered in v1 — their emitted sheet is skipped (shown in the receipt), not silently dropped.
fix.tier.alreadyTiered: Folder already ships resolution tiers — tiering skipped
fix.tier.badSuffix: Suffix "{suffix}" isn't a recognized resolution token — tiers wouldn't cluster on re-analysis
fix.tier.dedupConflict: Aggressive de-duplication and tiering both rename owners — reference repointing was disabled for this run
fix.tier.meshUnsupported: Atlas carries mesh sprites — scaling drops mesh geometry, so tiering was refused
fix.tier.multiPageSpine: Multi-page Spine atlas — tiering is limited to single-page Spine for now
fix.profile.title: Custom export variants
fix.profile.hint: Replaces the single format + tier ladder with your chosen resolutions × formats — one file per combination.
fix.profile.avifNoLossless: Browser AVIF has no true lossless mode — omitted (no faked-lossless claim).
fix.profile.tierBadSuffix: "{suffix}" isn't a recognized resolution token — variants wouldn't cluster on re-analysis
fix.profile.noBundleNote: v1 emits the variant files but not a bundle or atlas-data manifest yet — your loader still wires them up.
fix.profile.diskNote: This only fans out files on disk — the device downloads ONE variant, so it's a file count, never a saving (disk ≠ VRAM, invariant 5).
fix.profile.overridesHint: Override formats or quality for a folder prefix (e.g. fonts → AVIF 4:4:4).
fix.profile.pngLossyHint: Route PNG output through the opt-in pngquant backend (lossy-indexed re-compression) for a smaller download. DISK ONLY — a quantized PNG still decodes to full RGBA on the GPU, so VRAM is unchanged. Needs the pngquant backend op enabled + consented; otherwise a normal lossless PNG ships.
fix.pixiManifestHint: Adds manifest.json mapping every emitted image/sheet (and each resolution tier as its own alias) so a PixiJS game can load the whole output with Assets.init({ manifest }). Sheets list the .json/.atlas; Spine still needs pixi-spine. Off ⇒ no extra file.
fix.includeFileSizesHint: Adds AssetPack's progressSize (KB) to each manifest src so PixiJS shows accurate load progress. 'Uncompressed' = file size / 1024; 'Gzip' = gzipped size / 1024 (matches an HTTP gzip transport). Sizes reflect the actually-shipped file (a sheet's .json/.atlas sidecar; the final bytes after any pngquant/KTX2 step). Requires the PixiJS manifest. Off ⇒ today's bare-string src.
fix.hashFilenamesHint: Renames every emitted image/sheet AD references to name.<hash>.ext (hash = sha256 of the final bytes) so you can serve the optimized folder with immutable long-cache headers. Sheet .json/.atlas sidecars are repointed to the hashed image, then hashed themselves; the loader-migration snippet and the PixiJS manifest reference the hashed names. The skeleton, manifest.json, and loose images with no AD-owned referrer keep stable names. Off means today's filenames (byte-identical). Best paired with the PixiJS manifest.
fix.backend.title: Native ops (backend, opt-in)
fix.backend.hint: Some ops are impossible in the browser. With your consent, eligible pages are sent to your configured server, encoded, and added to the download. Everything else stays 100% local. Default OFF.
fix.backend.unconfigured: No backend configured — set an API base and activate a license to enable native ops.
fix.backend.ktx2: Offer KTX2 GPU compression for atlas/loose pages
fix.backend.ktx2Hint: When enabled and consented, eligible pages are uploaded to your server, encoded to .ktx2 (UASTC + Zstd, mipmaps), and added to the zip beside the normal image. The browser fix stays the default; this is an opt-in fallback for the one op browsers can't do.
fix.backend.pngquantHint: When enabled and consented, PNG pages marked 'Lossy PNG' in the export profile are uploaded to your server, re-compressed with pngquant (256-color indexed), and shipped in place of the lossless PNG. This is a SMALLER DOWNLOAD only — the image still decodes to full RGBA on the GPU, so VRAM is unchanged. If pngquant can't meet its quality floor the original is kept.
fix.backend.unreachable: Backend unreachable — native ops will be skipped and the browser image kept (an honest note appears in the receipt).
fix.backend.costZip: Your download gets LARGER: it ships both the .ktx2 and the normal image (so any GPU can load it).
fix.backend.costVram: The VRAM win applies ONLY on GPUs that support BC7/ASTC/ETC2; other GPUs fall back to the raster image.
fix.backend.costLoader: Your game must add the Pixi KTX2 loader (import 'pixi.js/ktx2') — a one-time code change. The libktx transcoder loads from the Pixi CDN by default (self-host optional via setKTXTranscoderPath).
fix.backend.costPngquant: Smaller download only: the lossy PNG replaces the lossless one in place (same filename, drop-in). It decodes to full RGBA on the GPU, so VRAM is UNCHANGED.
fix.backend.consent: I understand these images will be uploaded to the server for encoding (processed in memory, not stored).

fix.backend.uploadCount.one: Up to {n} file would be uploaded:
fix.backend.uploadCount.other: Up to {n} files would be uploaded:

fix.backend.manifestAutoPaired: The PixiJS manifest is auto-enabled so your game can load the encoded files (otherwise the .ktx2 / re-compressed pages would ship with no loader wiring).
fix.backend.receipt: KTX2: {produced} of {uploaded} pages compressed on {host} (added beside the normal images).
fix.backend.receiptPngquant: pngquant: {produced} of {uploaded} PNG pages re-compressed on {host} — {before:bytes} → {after:bytes} download (in place; VRAM unchanged).
fix.backend.receiptFailed: {failed} page(s) fell back to the browser image (backend declined or unreachable).
fix.backend.receiptVram: KTX2 GPU VRAM ≤ {bytes:bytes} (worst case; less on GPUs that transcode to BC1/ETC1; raster fallback otherwise) — reported separately, not in the VRAM total.
fix.backend.receiptVramMeasured: Measured {measured:bytes} on your GPU (block-compressed) — down from {baseline:bytes} raster; ceiling ≤ {ceiling:bytes}. This device only.
fix.backend.receiptVramFallback: Your GPU has no block-compression support (or the transcoder didn't load) — KTX2 fell back to raster here, so there is no VRAM win on this device.
fix.backend.receiptLoader: To use the .ktx2 files your game must add the Pixi KTX2 loader (import 'pixi.js/ktx2'); the libktx transcoder loads from the Pixi CDN by default (self-host optional via setKTXTranscoderPath). The zip is larger because it also ships the normal images.
fix.backend.resampleHint: When enabled and consented, the full-resolution source of each downscaled scale-tier is uploaded to your server and downscaled with libvips' lanczos3 kernel — the one downscale kernel the browser canvas can't be asked for. The result replaces the browser tile at the SAME dimensions and format. This is a QUALITY option only: the file is the same size and decodes to full RGBA on the GPU, so disk and VRAM are unchanged. Not yet supported together with content-hash filenames.
fix.backend.costResample: Quality only: the lanczos3 tile replaces the browser tile in place (same dimensions, same format, same filename). It changes neither download size nor VRAM — only the receipt's measured high-frequency-content number.
fix.backend.receiptResample: resample: {produced} of {uploaded} tiles downscaled with lanczos3 on {host} (in place; same size, VRAM unchanged).
fix.backend.receiptResampleQuality: lanczos3 retained {pct:pct} more high-frequency content at the same file size (measured; not a sharpness verdict).
fix.backend.resampleTierHint: Tier downscales use libvips' lanczos3 kernel on your server this run (the browser tile is replaced at the same size); the in-browser resampler is the fallback if the backend is unavailable.
license.locked: Activate a license to unlock the Pro fix
license.err.inactive: This license is no longer active
license.err.seats_exceeded: All device seats are in use — deactivate one
license.err.rate_limited: Too many attempts — wait a minute
fix.settings.frameRedundancyHint: Pack byte-identical animation frames once and point every duplicate name at the shared region — a smaller sheet and less VRAM. Drop-in: every frame name still resolves. Exact VRAM, no estimate.
fix.settings.trimMarginHint: Tighten every untrimmed sprite to its opaque bounds inside a repack — a smaller sheet and less VRAM. Drop-in: every name still resolves. Exact VRAM, no estimate.

fix.framesAliased.one: Aliased {n} duplicate frame onto a shared region — VRAM {before:bytes} → {after:bytes} (all frame names still resolve)
fix.framesAliased.other: Aliased {n} duplicate frames onto a shared region — VRAM {before:bytes} → {after:bytes} (all frame names still resolve)

fix.crossSheetFramesDeduped.one: Deduped {n} duplicate frame across merged sheets onto a shared region — reclaimed {vram:bytes} VRAM (all frame names still resolve)
fix.crossSheetFramesDeduped.other: Deduped {n} duplicate frames across merged sheets onto a shared region — reclaimed {vram:bytes} VRAM (all frame names still resolve)

fix.crossSheetFramesDedupedDiskOnly.one: Deduped {n} duplicate frame across merged sheets onto a shared region — same VRAM tier, disk only (all frame names still resolve)
fix.crossSheetFramesDedupedDiskOnly.other: Deduped {n} duplicate frames across merged sheets onto a shared region — same VRAM tier, disk only (all frame names still resolve)

fix.trimmedOnRepack.one: Trimmed {n} untrimmed sprite to its opaque bounds — reclaimed {area} px, VRAM {before:bytes} → {after:bytes} (all names still resolve)
fix.trimmedOnRepack.other: Trimmed {n} untrimmed sprites to their opaque bounds — reclaimed {area} px, VRAM {before:bytes} → {after:bytes} (all names still resolve)
